title: prefill-decode: chunked speculative prefill + stage-overlap optimizations (kernel scheduler, KV cache, continuous batching)
author: Alex Kim
ci_status: pass (initial flaky integration test failed on first run, rerun passed)
release_notes: Runtime: Improved prefill->decode pipeline performance. Adds chunked speculative prefill, overlap of prefill/decode stages, kernel scheduler heuristics, and KV-cache micro-optimizations. Expect lower p95 latency and higher throughput for mixed-length workloads. Feature gated; rollout to dedicated clusters first.
description: Motivation: Prefill (key/value cache population) has been a major contributor to end-to-end generation latency for long-context and mixed-length workloads. This PR implements three coordinated optimizations: 1) chunked prefill where long prefill sequences are split into contiguous chunks to improve kernel locality and allow earlier decode overlap, 2) speculative prefill that issues lookahead prefill chunks for likely-following tokens to expose additional overlapping work, and 3) stage-overlap pipeline that overlaps prefill, KV-cache maintenance, and decode kernel execution with a lightweight kernel scheduler and continuous-batching integration. This is implemented behind a runtime feature flag (prefill_pipeline_v2) and is safe by default (speculation bounded, can be disabled per-model). Checklist: - [x] Chunked prefill implementation with chunk size heuristics - [x] Speculative prefill policy + bounded speculation window - [x] Kernel scheduler changes to prioritize small decode batches and overlap KV maintenance work - [x] KV-cache hot-path micro-optimizations (lock-free reads, reduced memcopies) - [x] Continuous batching integration and backpressure handling - [x] Unit + integration tests and regression benchmarks - [x] Canary results on dedicated perf cluster Design notes: - Chunking: long input sequences are split into configurable chunk_size (default 512 tokens). Each chunk runs a prefill pass; the decode stage can begin as soon as the first chunk's KV segments are ready. This reduces tail latency for streaming scenarios. - Speculation: a speculative_prefill window (default 1 chunk ahead) enqueues likely-next-chunk prefill jobs at low priority. Speculation is bounded; speculative results are discarded if model rolls back or tokenization diverges. - Scheduler: a lightweight scheduler prioritizes decode-ready small batches, evicts/merges KV-cache segments dynamically, and schedules maintenance tasks during idle GPU cycles. This reduces kernel launch overhead and improves occupancy. - KV-cache: refactored cache to reduce copies on insert/lookup and to make common reads lockless under the optimistic-path. Testing & safety: speculative prefill is disabled for models flagged non-deterministic; metrics are emitted for speculation hits/misses and extra work. Rollout plan: enable feature in dedicated clusters behind config, monitor telem (speculation_efficiency, p95_latency, throughput), then enable on hosted API for lower-risk models. See linked Linear tickets ENG-1892 and ENG-1901 for follow-ups and model gating.

bench_results: Mixed-length (50/50 mix short/long) canary on p4d: throughput +28% measured over 1h steady-state (baseline 18.2 tok/s -> 23.3 tok/s); p95 end-to-end latency down 18% (baseline 420ms -> 344ms)
Long-context (8k tokens) local perf: chunked prefill reduces p95 prefill walltime by 34% (baseline 920ms -> 606ms); end-to-end p95 down 22% when speculation enabled.
Small-batch decode (latency-sensitive) p50 improved 12%, p95 improved 15% due to scheduler prioritization and reduced kernel launch overhead.
Speculation hit rate observed 73% on canary traffic; when hit, decode latency improved by additional ~40ms on average. Speculation miss penalty < 10ms due to bounded window and fast discard path.
